MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 MiniMax H3 Image needs ComfyUI 0.45.0 or newer, the first version with these nodes. On an older ComfyUI the nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_image_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors14.6 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

The same text encoder as MiniMax H3 video: if you did Episode 41 you already have it.

 Load VAE

Download minimax_h3_image_vae_fp16.safetensors1.09 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 License

MiniMax H3 Image has its own license, the MiniMax-H3-Image Community License, separate from the MiniMax H3 video license. Read it and check what it says for your country before you use the model: some countries need a license from MiniMax first.

READ LICENSE MiniMax H3 Image model page 

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma: update to the latest version (these workflows need at least 1.4.183). A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

This is inpainting with a mask you paint yourself: paint over a part of your picture, write what happens there, and MiniMax H3 Image changes only that part. Apart from a soft edge around the mask, everything stays exactly your picture, at its own size. It is workflow 6 with a brush instead of a box, for when the shape matters. The demo takes the window out of a white wall.

 Steps

  1. Load your picture in Load Image Mini Pixaroma.
  2. On Inpaint Crop Pixaroma, click Open mask editor, paint over what to change and save. For the demo, paint over the window, both shutters and the ledge above it.
  3. Write what happens in the painted area in Prompt Pixaroma.
  4. Leave the seed on F to repeat a result, or switch it to R to try a new one every Run.
  5. Press Run. Drag across Image Compare Pixaroma to see before and after.

 Paint the mask first

This workflow opens with no mask. A painted mask is saved on your own PC, not inside the workflow file, so we cannot send ours along. If you press Run before painting, the whole picture goes through the model and comes back changed: in our test 80 to 90 % of its pixels were different. So paint first.

 Writing the prompt

  • To remove something, say what is there instead: Remove the window and its blue shutters in <Picture 1>, so the plain white wall continues in their place, flat and unbroken. <Picture 1> is the cut-out area, the only thing the model sees.
  • To change something, give the colour, the material and the shape of the new thing, and where it stands.
  • End with what to keep: Keep the rest of the white wall exactly as it is.
  • Name only things the cut-out area shows. Our first prompt ended with keep the roof and the blue door. Neither was inside the cut-out piece, and the model painted a blue door edge into it on 4 of 4 seeds.

 How it works

  • MiniMax H3 Image has no mask input, so the masking happens around it.
  • Inpaint Crop cuts out the painted area with some of the picture around it and makes it bigger, the model changes that piece, and Inpaint Stitch pastes back only the painted part, with a soft edge.

 Good to know

  • A plain remove does not remove. In the box workflow, Remove the window in <Picture 1>. left a window or a closed shutter on 4 of 4 seeds, and Remove the table drew another table on 4 of 4. With what is there instead written out, the window was gone on 4 of 4 here.
  • Paint a little more than the thing. Only the painted part is pasted back, so anything of the old thing left outside the mask stays in your picture: its ledge, its shadow, a hinge.
  • Only the area around the mask changes. We compared the four test results with the picture: farther than 200 px from the mask not one pixel was different.
  • Your picture keeps its size. Only the cut-out piece goes through the model, so the demo goes in and comes out at 1280 x 1280.
  • For a quick box instead of a painted mask, use workflow 6.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 Image) - MiniMax H3 Image, the picture model made by MiniMax itself. It is a different file from the H3 video models of Episode 41 and from P-H3 Image of Episode 42.
  • Load CLIP (MiniMax H3 text encoder) - Reads your prompt. It is the same Qwen3-VL 32B text encoder as MiniMax H3 video, so if you did Episode 41 you already have it. The type must be minimax.
  • Load VAE (MiniMax H3 Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. It is made for MiniMax H3 Image, a different file from the H3 video VAE and the P-H3 Image VAE.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your picture) - The picture to change. Click it to upload your own, or pick one from the list.
  • Inpaint Crop Pixaroma (2. paint the mask) - Click Open mask editor and paint over what to change. The node cuts out the painted area with 96 px of the picture around it and enlarges the piece to 1536 px on its long side, on the model's 32 pixel grid. Leave the numbers as they are.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (3. what happens in the mask) - Say what happens in the painted area, and what is there instead (see How to Use). <Picture 1> is the cut-out area.
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) repeats the result, R (random) tries a new one every Run. The demo uses seed 1.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs between the steps.

  • Inpaint Stitch Pixaroma (pastes it back) - Pastes the changed piece back into your picture: the painted area, with a wide soft edge around it (softness 96). Everything farther out is your original picture, pixel for pixel. If a faint patch shows, raise softness, or try a new seed.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • Get Image Size (the size of the cut-out area) - Reads the size of the cut-out area and hands it to the conditioning, so the changed piece comes out with the same size and shape.
  • MiniMax H3 Image Conditioning (prompt + the cut-out area) - Joins the prompt, the cut-out area and its size from Get Image Size. The model only ever sees this piece of your picture. The VAE wire anchors it in full detail.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (no negative prompt) - An empty negative. The model takes no negative prompt, and CFG stays at 1.
  • KSampler (6 steps, CFG 1) - The render: 6 steps, CFG 1, euler and simple, as MiniMax made the model. In our tests 10 steps made skin worse, and the er_sde sampler made it noisy, so leave these as they are.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the result) - Saves each result as PNG into ComfyUI/output/MiniMax H3 Image Inpaint and shows it on the node.
  • Image Compare Pixaroma (before and after, drag across it) - Your picture and the result on top of each other. Drag across it: only the painted area and its soft edge change.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: a smaller picture is faster.

WhatTime
target 1536 (the demo)about 5 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 35 GB: 19.5 GB for the model, 14.6 GB for the text encoder and 1 GB for the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it.

 On a smaller card

The cut-out piece is small, so the picture size is not what makes this workflow heavy: the models are. ComfyUI moves what does not fit on the card into your PC's memory, which is slower.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
